note: Dial hints, not authority. An entry here can send you to the wrong machine and cannot make you trust it: a peer id is sha256 of its McEliece transport key, so the handshake decides who answered and this file decides nothing. That is why publishing it on GitHub Pages is safe, and why losing GitHub Pages costs a hint rather than the network. See docs/discovery.md.
key_files: seeds/<transport>.key, relative to this file: the hex transport public key, 522240 characters. The file is named by the sha256 of the bytes it decodes to, so `cairn seeds` checks the name against the content and refuses a mismatch.

seeds.name: us-west
seeds.note: Key published by `cairn seeds publish` on the seed host and added by pull request; the file beside this list is named for the sha256 of its bytes and `cairn seeds resolve` re-derives that id before writing a bootstrap file. p2p dials addr directly and the handshake decides who answered. The http half is a mirror, not a live endpoint: the node serves plain HTTP and terminates no TLS by design, so workflows/node-sync.yml pulls its read endpoints every five minutes and re-serves them under /node/ on this site. The site is therefore at most one interval behind, and the reader re-derives the log either way -- it is hash-linked and carries a signed checkpoint. While the node is down the site keeps the last copy; before the first sync it serves nothing under /node/ and the reader falls back to the bundled launch log, labeled as such.
